walkthroughs.body_html:
Themes in the Synoptic Gospels — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Themes in the Synoptic Gospels brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Themes in the Synoptic Gospels.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which gospels are known as the synoptic gospels?
options: Matthew, Mark and Luke
Matthew, Mark and John
Mark, Luke and John
Matthew, Luke and John
Mark was written first and used as a source by Matthew and Luke
Mark is the most theologically important gospel
Mark was written by Peter himself
Mark was the last gospel to be written
A hypothesised sayings source behind material common to Matthew and Luke but not found in Mark
The oldest complete manuscript of Mark
A lost gospel quoted in John
An abbreviation for the Greek word for gospel

mcqs.q: What is the parable of the sower about?
options: Different responses to the message of the kingdom
The return of a lost son
Paying taxes to Caesar
The rebuilding of the Temple

mcqs.q: Were the gospels written down as eyewitness diaries at the time of the events?
options: No - they were composed decades later (Mark is commonly dated around AD 65-75), drawing on oral tradition and earlier sources shaped for particular communities.
Parables are historical reports of real named individuals.
The gospels were written a thousand years after Jesus.
The gospels were written word for word as Jesus spoke, like court transcripts.

mcqs.q: Do differences between the synoptic gospels mean random copying errors?
options: Any difference between Matthew, Mark and Luke is just an accidental mistake.
Parables are historical reports of real named individuals.
Not usually - each evangelist selected, arranged and emphasised material for a particular audience and theological purpose, which redaction criticism studies.
The three gospels were written by the same person under different names.

mcqs.q: Are parables simply children's stories with easy morals?
options: Parables are historical reports of real named individuals.
Parables are straightforward moral fables that anyone immediately understands.
The three gospels were written by the same person under different names.
No - parables are often subversive, demand a decision about the kingdom, and Mark 4 even presents them as concealing as well as revealing meaning.
